idiom_name: Thread.new fan-out + Thread#value/join in ensure + flag-based cooperative stop
implementation_notes: Ruby ships primitives, not scopes: start children with Thread.new, join them with Thread#value (which returns the child's result or re-raises its exception in the caller), and repeat the join set in an ensure block so no exit path leaves a thread behind. Cancellation must be cooperative - a shared flag or Thread::Queue signal that children poll - because Thread#raise/Thread#kill interrupt at arbitrary points and are only safe inside Thread.handle_interrupt; Thread.report_on_exception (true by default since Ruby 2.5) prints unhandled child exceptions but does not propagate them.
code_sketch:
threads = urls.map { |url| Thread.new { fetch(url) } }
begin
  results = threads.map(&:value)   # value joins; re-raises a child's failure
ensure
  threads.each(&:join)             # the scope cannot exit before its children
end
pitfalls: A child that is never joined is left running, and with report_on_exception its failure may print later, out of context; the ensure-join set is what makes the scope real.
Thread#raise and Thread#kill can corrupt invariants by interrupting a thread anywhere; coordinate with a flag instead.
The GVL means CPU-bound threads do not run in parallel - use processes or native extensions when the scope is meant to parallelize CPU work.
